engine_name: Cross-Scene Continuity Graph & Impact Propagation Director
purpose: Build and traverse the canonical dependency graph across scenes, characters, events, assets and world state so any approved change produces a deterministic impact set, invalidation scope and revalidation/regeneration plan.
core_principle: A canonical change propagates through causally dependent nodes, never through arbitrary similarity.

change_classes.IDENTITY_CHANGE: Character immutable identity or visual identity change.
change_classes.STATE_CHANGE: Character emotional, knowledge, relationship or behavioral state change.
change_classes.EVENT_CHANGE: Canonical event transition or causal outcome change.
change_classes.WORLD_CHANGE: Persistent environmental, spatial or world-state change.
change_classes.ASSET_CHANGE: Asset master, costume, prop, VFX or continuity asset changes.

invalidation_policy: Canonical source nodes are never deleted by propagation.
Derived nodes become INVALIDATED only when their dependency fingerprint no longer matches.
Inactive narrative branches remain preserved but are not promoted into the active impact frontier.
A changed master asset invalidates dependent derivatives, not unrelated assets.
A state change propagates only to scenes whose canonical state derives from that state.
A world-state change propagates through persistent locations and re-entry scenes.
An event change propagates through downstream causal events and dependent scene masters.
Impact propagation must be deterministic and auditable.

severity_rules.CRITICAL: Canonical identity, branch, timeline, causal event or master fingerprint change affects production truth.
severity_rules.HIGH: Persistent character/world state or trusted master asset affects dependent scenes.
severity_rules.MEDIUM: Frame, costume, prop, VFX, audio or camera derivative requires revalidation or regeneration.
severity_rules.LOW: Non-canonical production metadata or presentation-only derivative.

revalidation_frontier.ordering: Topological dependency order; critical-path nodes first.

rules: No active derivative may depend on a superseded canonical node.
No cycle may exist in causal dependency edges.
Every propagated impact must have a source change and dependency path.
Every invalidated derivative must have an explicit recovery action.
Branch-inactive nodes cannot create active production work.
Scene active-character constraints remain maximum five.
